subject.title: [Bug]: Enabling Codex plugin causes Runtime to switch to OpenAI Codex and ignore configured primary model, resulting in GPT-5.4-nano TPM failures

question: Should #99449 be fixed as a narrow stale OpenAI route/doctor-owner repair first, folded entirely into #87957's shared session-state resolver, or treated as expected when the session explicitly selected OpenAI with better diagnostics?
rationale: Source shows DeepSeek should not be claimed directly by Codex, but the live report mixes Codex hot reload, persisted selected model state, and an explicit `/model openai` clarification, so maintainer intent is needed before choosing the durable session-state contract.

options.title: Fix narrow route drift first
options.body: Repair stale auto OpenAI session pins and literal OpenAI doctor ownership for non-OpenAI primaries while keeping #87957 as the broader resolver tracker.

options.title: Fold into #87957
options.body: Use the shared session model/auth resolver tracker as the sole implementation path and copy this DeepSeek/Codex hot-reload scenario into its acceptance criteria before closing later.

options.title: Clarify explicit OpenAI behavior
options.body: If maintainers decide the observed route follows the user's explicit `/model openai` selection, keep OpenAI-to-Codex behavior and improve status or doctor messaging instead of changing routing.

recommendation.title: Fix narrow route drift first
recommendation.body: Repair stale auto OpenAI session pins and literal OpenAI doctor ownership for non-OpenAI primaries while keeping #87957 as the broader resolver tracker.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest feature-history trail across OpenAI provider identity and shared session model resolution decisions.
